# Net

Networking: IP and socket addresses, TCP listeners and streams, UDP sockets, and name resolution.

## Installation

Add `Net` to the `[Dependencies]` table of your package's `Rux.toml`:

```toml
[Dependencies]
Net = { Namespace = "Rux", Version = "0.1.0" }
```

Standard packages are declared by hand: the registry does not serve them, so `rux add Rux/Net` cannot add them.

## Dependencies

- [`Allocator`](/docs/api/allocator) 0.1.0
- [`Collections`](/docs/api/collections) 0.1.0
- [`Core`](/docs/api/core) 0.1.0
- [`FreeBSD`](/docs/api/freebsd) 0.1.0 (FreeBSD only)
- [`Io`](/docs/api/io) 0.1.0
- [`Linux`](/docs/api/linux) 0.1.0 (Linux only)
- [`macOS`](/docs/api/macos) 0.1.0 (macOS only)
- [`Text`](/docs/api/text) 0.1.0
- [`Time`](/docs/api/time) 0.1.0
- [`Windows`](/docs/api/windows) 0.1.0 (Windows only)

## Guide

Networking: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, TCP listeners and streams, UDP sockets, and host name resolution.

### What it provides

| Module                                     | Covers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Address`                                  | [`Ipv4Address`](/docs/api/net/address#ipv4-address), [`Ipv6Address`](/docs/api/net/address#ipv6-address), [`IpAddress`](/docs/api/net/address#ip-address) and [`SocketAddress`](/docs/api/net/address#socket-address), each with `Parse`, `WriteText`, `Equals` and `Display`                                                                                  |
| `Tcp`                                      | [`TcpListener`](/docs/api/net/tcp#tcp-listener) with `Bind`, [`Accept`](/docs/api/net/tcp#accept) and `LocalAddress`; [`TcpStream`](/docs/api/net/tcp#tcp-stream), an `Io` reader and writer, with `Connect`, [`Shutdown`](/docs/api/net/tcp#shutdown), [`SetNoDelay`](/docs/api/net/tcp#set-no-delay) and timeouts; `SetNonBlocking` and `PollSource` on both |
| `Udp`                                      | [`UdpSocket`](/docs/api/net/udp#udp-socket) with `Bind`, [`SendTo`](/docs/api/net/udp#send-to), [`ReceiveFrom`](/docs/api/net/udp#receive-from), `Connect`, [`Send`](/docs/api/net/udp#send), [`Receive`](/docs/api/net/udp#receive), a read timeout, `SetNonBlocking` and `PollSource`; [`Datagram`](/docs/api/net/udp#datagram)                              |
| [`Resolve`](/docs/api/net/resolve#resolve) | [`Resolve`](/docs/api/net/resolve#resolve), the addresses of a host name                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Dns`                                      | [`Resolver`](/docs/api/net/resolver), a DNS client with [`WithServers`](/docs/api/net/resolver#with-servers), [`FromSystem`](/docs/api/net/resolver#from-system), [`SetTimeout`](/docs/api/net/resolver#set-timeout), [`SetAttempts`](/docs/api/net/resolver#set-attempts) and [`Lookup`](/docs/api/net/resolver#lookup)                                       |
| `Poll`                                     | [`Poller`](/docs/api/net/poller) with [`Register`](/docs/api/net/poller#register), [`Modify`](/docs/api/net/poller#modify), [`Deregister`](/docs/api/net/poller#deregister) and [`Wait`](/docs/api/net/poller#wait); [`Interest`](/docs/api/net/poller#interest), `PollSource` and [`PollEvent`](/docs/api/net/poller#poll-event)                              |

The module names describe where each declaration comes from; they are not part of an import path.

### Example

```rux
import Allocator::SystemAllocator;
import Io::{ IoError, ReadExact, WriteAll };
import Net::{ Resolve, TcpStream };

func Greet(host: char8[..]) -> ! IoError {
    let addresses = Resolve(SystemAllocator(), host, 7)?;
    var stream = TcpStream::Connect(addresses.AsSlice()[0])?;
    WriteAll(stream, "hello")?;
    var echoed: char8[5] = ['\0'; 5];
    ReadExact(stream, echoed[..])?;
}
```

### Design

Sockets block by default: a call waits until it can do its work, or until the timeout set for it runs out and it fails with `TimedOut`. `SetNonBlocking` makes a socket's calls fail with `WouldBlock` instead whenever they would wait, and a [`Poller`](/docs/api/net/poller) says when they would not: sockets are registered with a token and the readiness wanted, and [`Wait`](/docs/api/net/poller#wait) reports the ready ones by token, waiting up to a timeout. It is level-triggered, so a socket is reported for as long as it is ready, and runs on epoll on Linux, kqueue on FreeBSD and macOS, and `WSAPoll` on Windows. A stream a listener accepts starts blocking whatever the listener is. Failures are `Io::IoError` values, so a [`TcpStream`](/docs/api/net/tcp#tcp-stream) passes straight to anything that takes an `Io` reader or writer, and the reasons a connection fails — refused, reset, aborted, unreachable, an address in use — have kinds of their own. Writing to a connection the peer has closed fails with `BrokenPipe` rather than ending the process with a signal. Every socket is closed when its value is dropped, and none is inherited by a child process.

Addresses are plain values. IPv4 addresses are read in the four-part decimal form only, without the leading zeros some systems read as octal; IPv6 addresses take the `::` shorthand and an embedded IPv4 tail, and are written as RFC 5952 asks, in lower case with the longest run of zeros shortened and an IPv4-mapped address with its IPv4 tail, as in `::ffff:192.0.2.1`. A socket address writes an IPv6 address in brackets, as in `[::1]:8080`. Every address type also renders through `{}`, padded to the placeholder's width, and answers `IsLoopback`, `IsUnspecified`, `IsPrivate` (RFC 1918, or a unique local IPv6 address), `IsLinkLocal` and `IsMulticast`.

On Linux and FreeBSD the sockets are system calls. On macOS they come from libSystem and on Windows from Winsock, which is started the first time a socket is opened. On FreeBSD, macOS and Windows [`Resolve`](/docs/api/net/resolve#resolve) asks the system's resolver, `getaddrinfo`, so names resolve as they do for every other program on the machine. On Linux that resolver belongs to the C library, so [`Resolve`](/docs/api/net/resolve#resolve) reads `/etc/hosts` and asks the name servers in `/etc/resolv.conf` itself, and a program that resolves names stays a static binary; search domains and the name service switch are not followed. [`Resolver`](/docs/api/net/resolver) is that DNS client, usable on every system with servers of the caller's choosing: it asks each server in turn for the IPv4 and then the IPv6 addresses over UDP, and over TCP when an answer is too long for a datagram. A numeric host is read directly.
